title: Beauty eCommerce: How To Win Across Every Channel
summary: Beauty ecommerce means DTC, marketplaces, retailer dropship, and social at once. See how consistent product data keeps every channel selling.
body_markdown:
In this article, learn about:


-


Why beauty ecommerce behaves like a channel portfolio instead of a storefront


-


What the digital shelf has to carry when a shopper can't test the product


-


How retailer dropship differs from direct-to-consumer (DTC) and marketplace fulfillment


---


The channel mix in beauty is changing quickly. TD Cowen expects[Amazon to grow from 10% of the US beauty market in 2024 to 15% by 2030](https://www.retaildive.com/news/beauty-growth-amazon-tiktok-shop-market-share/745231/) and TikTok Shop to climb from 1% to 3%, while drug stores slide from 5% to 3% and department stores from 7% to 5%. The beauty sector keeps growing at roughly 5% a year through 2030, against a US market worth about $115 billion once wellness is included.


That shift changes what a health, beauty, and wellness (HBW) brand should focus on. Selling beauty products online requires a portfolio of channels, and each one has its own fulfillment model, data format, and rules.


**Related Reading:**[The Health, Beauty, and Wellness Category: A Brand's Guide to Selling and Scaling in Retail](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/the-health-beauty-and-wellness-category-a-brands-guide-to-selling-and-scaling-in-retail) **

This is why a brand can be great on its own site and still struggle when a retailer dot-com goes live, since the data and fulfillment work have different requirements.


## What Does the Digital Shelf Do When Selling Beauty Products Online?


The digital shelf is all the content that represents a product online, such as images, copy, ingredients, attributes, certifications, and reviews. The digital shelf matters more in beauty than in almost any other category; online, a shopper can't swatch a foundation, smell a fragrance, or read the panel on a supplement bottle as they can in a store.


The hardest difficulty is attribute depth. For instance, one complexion product can ship in 40 shades, with each shade requiring its own name, undertone, image, and stock-keeping unit (SKU). Skincare adds ingredient lists, claims, and certifications, and supplements add serving sizes and panel data. That is far more data per item than most categories need, and it grows with every variant.


Format is the other half of the problem. A single retailer could want a shade as free text, while another could want it mapped to a set list. Marketplaces will reject items outright when a required field is missing. Brands that manage this in spreadsheets end up with a different version of their data on every channel.


## How Does Retailer Dropship Differ From Other Fulfillment Models?


On its own site, a brand controls the whole flow and pays the full cost, while on a marketplace, it can ship each order itself or send stock in advance.


Retailer dropship is where a growing brand usually hits real complexity. Dropshipping is when the retailer takes the consumer order, and the brand ships it to that shopper in packing slips and labels carrying the retailer's brand.[Direct-to-consumer fulfillment runs on electronic data interchange (EDI)](https://www.spscommerce.com/drop-shipping/suppliers/) , and the document set is long. Inventory updates often flow several times a day, and retailers want the ASN on every order because it gives the shopper tracking information.


Additionally, retailers ask dropship suppliers for much more item detail than they ask of suppliers shipping into a distribution center, since the retailer website has to sell a product it’s never holding in stock.


## What Issues Do Beauty and Wellness Brands Have That Other Sectors Do Not?


Three issues cause most of the surprises for HBW brands, and all three sit with the brand, its counsel, its carriers, and specialist logistics providers.


### Fragrance and Aerosols Are Regulated Hazardous Materials


Most alcohol-based fragrance is a[Class 3 flammable liquid](https://nicecommerce.com/blogs/the-nice-way/shipping-perfume-hazmat-guide) , which means it ignites at or below 60 degrees Celsius, and aerosols are pressurized gases. Shipping either one legally takes UN-rated packaging, hazmat labels, paperwork, carrier approval, and trained staff.


Most standard 3PL warehouses will not handle these products, leading to brands with a fragrance line often running two fulfillment operations. Marketplaces also run a dangerous-goods review before a listing goes live, and mistakes can mean seized packages, carrier fines, or a closed account.


### Dated Products Run Into Marketplace Shelf-Life Rules


Marketplaces set a minimum remaining shelf life on the stock they accept. Amazon, for instance, says a unit must arrive with enough life left to be used up in full, plus another 90 days. Some marketplaces set stricter limits.


The date printed on a batch decides which channels will take it. A batch with eight months of life left may be fine for a wholesale retailer and still be refused at a marketplace fulfillment center, so a brand has to know which batch is going to which channel before it ships.


### Claim and Labeling Rules Apply to Every Listing


The rules that govern claims on a package also govern the product page, the bullet points, and the attribute fields. A claim that would not pass on a carton is no safer in a marketplace description.


A checklist before any new listing goes live:


-


Confirmed hazmat classification and a fulfillment partner approved to ship it


-


Remaining shelf life that clears the channel's intake threshold


-


Claims and ingredient data reviewed against the same standard as the physical label


-


Required attributes complete in that channel's format, not only in the brand's own


**Related Reading:**[Ingredient Disclosure and "Clean Beauty" Standards](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/ingredient-disclosure-and-clean-beauty-standards)


## How Do You Keep Inventory and Product Data Consistent Everywhere?


Selling on multiple channels intensifies every inventory error. The same unit can be promised to a marketplace shopper, a retailer dot-com order, and a wholesale purchase order in one hour. Social-driven demand can clear weeks of stock in days.


The pattern shows up on the retail side of the network too. GNC is the largest specialty health and wellness retailer, and it sells through stores, its own site, and marketplaces. Before working with SPS Commerce, GNC could not say how many units it had in stock, because the data sat in separate departments. Its ASN compliance rate had fallen to 76%. In a little over a year it[rose to 92%, and inventory performed better](https://www.spscommerce.com/resources/case-study-gnc-scpm/) .


"With SPS, we have true visibility into our entire operation," said Marty Hahn, director of vendor relations at GNC. Brands that scale online treat product content, inventory, and order data as one system that every channel reads from. The alternative is five copies kept by hand.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Do I need EDI to sell on a retailer's website?


Usually, yes. Retailer dropship programs run on EDI documents, including the purchase order, the acknowledgment, the advance ship notice, and the invoice. Some smaller retailers accept a supplier portal, though portals stop scaling as volume grows.


### Can I use my current 3PL for fragrance and aerosols?


Only if it is set up for hazardous materials. This work needs certified training, UN-rated packaging, and carrier approval, so many brands use a specialist hazmat provider for those items.


### How much product data does a marketplace actually require?


More than a brand's own site, and in a fixed shape. Each channel publishes its own taxonomy and required attributes. An item missing a required field is usually rejected rather than published incomplete.
